description:
Junior AI Vision & Automation Engineer – Automotive Manufacturing
Vance, AL
Full Time
Entry Level
 SHARE
SWJ Technology specializes in providing engineering, planning, and project management services across various industries. We are currently seeking a Junior AI Vision & Automation Engineer – Automotive Manufacturing a client in the automotive industry, specializing in car manufacturing. This role is a contractor position based in Vance, AL that requires onsite presence.  If you’re eager to grow your career and make a meaningful impact on exciting projects, we look forward to your application.
 
PURPOSE: 
The role supports the development, implementation, programming, and maintenance of AI-based vision systems and collaborative robots (cobots) in automotive manufacturing.
The position focuses on digitalizing and automating quality inspection and production processes across Body, Paint, and Assembly. The successful candidate will work alongside experienced engineers and develop practical skills in AI applications, software development, industrial automation, and robotics.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
AI Vision & Software Development:
Support the implementation, configuration, and testing of AI-based camera and video recognition systems.
Assist with training and improving AI models for automated quality inspections.
Develop and modify basic software applications using Python, JavaScript, or Node-RED.
Support database management, dashboards, and production data analysis.
Cobot Programming & Automation:
Support programming, configuration, and commissioning of collaborative robots (cobots).
Develop and adjust basic robot movements, positions, and operating sequences.
Assist with integrating cameras, AI vision systems, and robotic applications.
Support testing, troubleshooting, and optimization of automated processes.
Production & Project Support:
Support implementation of AI and automation solutions in Body, Paint, and Assembly.
Assist with troubleshooting and continuous improvement of production processes.
Coordinate technical activities with production, quality, engineering, and IT teams.
Prepare technical documentation and support system users.
QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor's or master's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline.
Recent university graduates are welcome.
Initial practical experience through internships, university projects, or technical assignments is an advantage.
No extensive professional experience required..

REQUIRED SKILLS:
Technical Knowledge:
Basic programming knowledge in Python, JavaScript, C++, or similar languages
Basic understanding of software development, data processing, and computer systems
Interest in AI, machine learning, computer vision, and video recognition.
Basic understanding of automation, robotics, or electrical/mechanical systems.
Initial experience with cobots or industrial robots is beneficial, but not mandatory.
Familiarity with Node-RED, Ignition, or SQL is an advantage.
Willingness to learn new software platforms and industrial technologies.
Personal Requirements:
Strong technical interest and willingness to learn.
Analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
Hands-on mentality and practical approach to engineering.
Good communication and teamwork skills.
Structured and independent working style.
Good English skills; German is an advantage due to international project cooperation.
PREFERRED SKILLS:
Knowledge of automotive manufacturing processes (Body, Paint, Assembly).
Familiarity with Mercedes-Benz Production System (MPS), Q-Live, INQA, or FAMOUS stations.
Initial experience with AI-based inspection systems, industrial cameras, sensors, or automation.
Interest in digital manufacturing and continuous improvement.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Work is normally performed in an office, laboratory, manufacturing floor, or machine shop setting where physical work includes, but is not limited to sitting, standing, reaching, kneeling, bending, and lifting up to 25 lbs.
Must be able to understand and comply with all relevant safety practices.
FLSA STATUS/WORKING SCHEDULE:
Location: Vance, AL
Schedule: Day shift, 40h/w, weekend as required
Overtime: as required
Assignment Start: ASAP

DISCLAIMER:
This job description is a high-level overview of general expectations of this position. It is not intended to list every responsibility of the position, nor does it represent an employment contract of any kind.

Why are you being asked to complete this form?

We are a federal contractor or subcontractor. The law requires us to provide equal employment opportunity to qualified people with disabilities. We have a goal of having at least 7% of our workers as people with disabilities. The law says we must measure our progress towards this goal. To do this, we must ask applicants and employees if they have a disability or have ever had one. People can become disabled, so we need to ask this question at least every five years.

Completing this form is voluntary, and we hope that you will choose to do so. Your answer is confidential. No one who makes hiring decisions will see it. Your decision to complete the form and your answer will not harm you in any way. If you want to learn more about the law or this form, visit the U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) website at www.dol.gov/ofccp.

How do you know if you have a disability?

A disability is a condition that substantially limits one or more of your “major life activities.” If you have or have ever had such a condition, you are a person with a disability. Disabilities include, but are not limited to:

Alcohol or other substance use disorder (not currently using drugs illegally)
Autoimmune disorder, for example, lupus, fibromyalgia, rheumatoid arthritis, HIV/AIDS
Blind or low vision
Cancer (past or present)
Cardiovascular or heart disease
Celiac disease
Cerebral palsy
Deaf or serious difficulty hearing
Diabetes
Disfigurement, for example, disfigurement caused by burns, wounds, accidents, or congenital disorders
Epilepsy or other seizure disorder
Gastrointestinal disorders, for example, Crohn's Disease, irritable bowel syndrome
Intellectual or developmental disability
Mental health conditions, for example, depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety disorder, schizophrenia, PTSD
Missing limbs or partially missing limbs
Mobility impairment, benefiting from the use of a wheelchair, scooter, walker, leg brace(s) and/or other supports
Nervous system condition, for example, migraine headaches, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis (MS)
Neurodivergence, for example, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia, dyspraxia, other learning disabilities
Partial or complete paralysis (any cause)
Pulmonary or respiratory conditions, for example, tuberculosis, asthma, emphysema
Short stature (dwarfism)
Traumatic brain injury
